subject: Tiered private offer: usage add-ons, partner uplift and passback mechanics
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@cloudbuyer.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudservices.co
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer structure questions and partner uplift

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — CloudBuyer is excited to move forward. Before we pull procurement into the PO flow, a couple of clarifying questions around the private offer you shared:

1) We expect some customers to purchase committed capacity + usage-based add-ons (e.g., overage or burst credits). How should those add-ons be priced in the private offer so that our channel partners can still take their commission/fee?

2) We typically require a partner uplift (a small uplift to list to compensate our reseller network). Can Redwood support a partner uplift on the private offer and still preserve the list-price / marketplace reporting requirements?

3) Are you able to provide a sample channel passback scenario if we structure three tiers (50k, 150k, 500k monthly committed usage) with metered overage?

Procurement would like to see a sample PO and an example of how credits / overage credits would be handled on invoices. I attached our internal purchasing template for reference.

Thanks — can you loop in the channel/finance folks so we can get a concrete example?

Best,
Rajiv
CloudBuyer, Inc.
rajiv.mehta@cloudbuyer.com
[Attachment: CloudBuyer_PO_Template.docx (docx)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@cloudbuyer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer structure questions and partner uplift

Thanks Rajiv — looping in Ben (channel) and Irene (revenue ops) to provide concrete passback numbers and invoice behavior. Initial thoughts below, happy to refine based on what procurement needs: 

- Private offer model: we can create a committed-tier structure that defines a list price for each tier and a separate metered SKU for overage/burst. The private offer will surface both SKUs so your partner uplift can apply to the line item you designate (committed or net revenue per our agreement).

- Partner uplift options: we support an uplift applied as either (A) a list-price multiplier (e.g., +6% to list visible in marketplace metadata) or (B) an explicit resell-credit line item on the invoice (keeps marketplace list untouched). Option B is cleaner for marketplace reporting but requires invoice-level passback.

- Overage handling: overages can be billed monthly with a pre-defined credit / threshold. We can issue retroactive credits if you prefer monthly smoothing. Need to decide whether partner commission applies to gross overage or post-credit net.

I've attached a first-pass pricing workbook (RBW-pricing-draft.xlsx) with scenario placeholders and three tier examples. Ben/Irene — can you review and populate recommended passback percentages and confirm tax/withholding implications?

Next steps for us: once we align on passback method and uplift approach, I can generate a draft private offer and PO to share with your procurement.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RBW-pricing-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer structure questions and partner uplift

On Sat, Jun 5, 2027 at 10:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a first-pass pricing workbook... Ben/Irene — can you review and populate recommended passback percentages and confirm tax/withholding implications?

Quick pass from channel / commissions perspective:

- Recommended passback approach: invoice-level passback (Option B from Mina). Rationale: keeps marketplace list price stable for reporting and avoids creating multiple observable list prices that complicate comparability.

- Tiered commission suggestion (applies to net revenue after any customer-facing credits):
  * Tier A (<= $50k/mo committed): 8% passback to partner
  * Tier B ($50k-$150k): 6% passback
  * Tier C (>$150k): 4% passback

- Metered overage SKU: treat as a separate line item with 5% passback to partner (applies to billed overage net of credits).

- Partner uplift handling: instead of adjusting the marketplace list price, add a 'Partner Uplift' invoice line to the private offer. That way procurement sees a single private-offer total and partners receive their uplift without list changes.

- Tax/withholding: Irene, please confirm but expect partner remit rules to vary by region — if CloudBuyer remits partner payout we can invoice net and passback via monthly settlement. For US customers this is straightforward; EU may need VAT handling on the uplift.

Attached is a short scenario deck with example invoices to illustrate the passback.

Ben Carter
Director, Channel & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: channel-passback-scenarios.pdf (pdf)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@cloudbuyer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, procurement@cloudservices.co
Date: 2027-06-07T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer structure questions and partner uplift

Rajiv — thanks for the detailed questions and patience while we pulled ops and channel in. Summary / agreed approach below: 

1) Structure: private offer with two SKUs per seat/instance: Committed-tier SKU + Metered overage SKU. Both SKUs appear in the private offer so usage is transparent.

2) Partner uplift and passback: Redwood will not modify marketplace list price. Instead we will add a discrete 'Partner Uplift' invoice line that settles monthly to your partner. Passback percentages will be invoice-line based per Ben's proposal: Tiered passback (8% / 6% / 4%) on committed net revenue and 5% on metered overage.

3) Credits & smoothing: We can implement monthly smoothing for overage credits. Overage is billed monthly and we will apply pre-agreed credits before calculating passback.

4) Next steps:
  - I will generate a draft private offer and sample PO that reflects the invoice-line uplift model and send it to procurement.
  - Rajiv / procurement: please confirm whether you need partner uplift to be paid to CloudBuyer or to a named reseller; we will need the payout remit details to configure settlements.
  - Finance check: Irene, can you confirm EU VAT handling if payout flows to a European partner?

I've attached the draft private offer (CloudBuyer_PrivateOffer_PO_v1.pdf) and the RBW workbook. If this looks good I can convert to a DocuSign-ready PO and file the HubSpot record HS-78901.

Appreciate it — looking forward to closing the PO ASAP.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: CloudBuyer_PrivateOffer_PO_v1.pdf (pdf)]
